submitted.rationale: With only 3 merit measurements, I targeted the Cu-modified BiVO4 region (the best-known visible-light photoanode, able to absorb 2.72 eV photons) and included one Cu-V-rich probe as a contrast. Index 0 (Bi0.36 Cu0.18 V0.46, slightly V-rich relative to 1:1 Bi:V, low Cu) gave the highest photocurrent at 2.65e-5 A. That is about twice index 34 (near-stoichiometric Bi:V) and about ten times the Cu-V-rich index 2.

rejected.reason: Measured 1.26e-5 A. Close to 1:1 Bi:V but lower than the slightly V-rich index 0.
Measured 2.2e-6 A. The Cu-V-rich (CuV2O6-like) region performs poorly.
Cu-rich oxides are expected to be poor photoanodes, and the Cu-V probe supports this. Not measured because the budget was limited.
